topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
sections.content: Define a planar graph as one that can be drawn in a plane without edges crossing. Introduce the basic components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F).
sections.example: A simple triangle graph (3 vertices, 3 edges, 2 faces: one internal, one external 'infinite' face).

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Euler's Characteristic Formula
sections.content: Introduce the formula V - E + F = 2. Explain how this invariant property holds true for any connected planar graph, regardless of how complex the network looks.
sections.example: Visual animation showing a square (V=4, E=4, F=2) transforming into a complex shape—the sum 4-4+2 always remains 2.

sections.title: Concept of the Dual Graph
sections.content: Explain the construction of a dual graph: place a point in each face of the original graph and connect points if their faces share an edge.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Spider-Man Web' graph. Placing nodes in each web-gap and connecting them creates a dual 'Constellation' graph, illustrating the mapping process.

sections.title: The Relationship Between Primal and Dual
sections.content: Demonstrate the mathematical link: V_dual = F_primal, F_dual = V_primal, and E_dual = E_primal. This inversion shows why the formula is symmetric.
sections.example: A 'Robot Circuit Board' layout: showing how swapping components (vertices) and wires (edges) maintains the logical topology of the circuit.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Wrap up by explaining why duality matters in map coloring problems and printed circuit board (PCB) design to minimize edge crossings.
sections.example: A Map of Countries: Turning countries into nodes and borders into edges shows how graph duality simplifies geographic network analysis.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Planar graphs have no intersecting edges.
Faces are regions bounded by Edges.
Consider the infinite exterior region as a face.
animations: Fade in a simple graph with 3 vertices and 3 edges (a triangle). Color: #FFFFFF.
Label vertices V=3, edges E=3, faces F=1. Color: #FFD700.
Highlight edges to show they don't cross in a plane. Color: #00FF00.
Fade in a second graph that does cross (K3,3). Color: #FF4500.
Highlight intersection point to prove non-planarity. Color: #FF0000.

storyboard.title: The Golden Rule: Euler's Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula defines a fundamental invariant.
Sum Vertices, subtract Edges, add Faces.
For connected graphs, this equals two.
It holds regardless of graph complexity.
The value two always remains constant.
animations: Display formula: V - E + F = 2. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate substituting V=3, E=3, F=2 for the triangle. Color: #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: Concept of the Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Construct dual graphs by placing points.
Place a point in every face.
Connect points if faces share edges.
animations: Display a primal graph in #FFFFFF and place a new vertex in each face. Color: #FFD700.
Draw edges between dual vertices if primal faces share an edge. Color: #00FF00.
Fade out the primal graph, leaving only the dual graph. Color: #FFD700.

storyboard.title: The Relationship Between Primal and Dual
lecture_lines: Primal Vertices map to Dual Faces.
Primal Edges map to Dual Edges.
Primal Faces map to Dual Vertices.
animations: Show primal and dual graphs side-by-side. Color: #FFFFFF and #FFD700.
Highlight primal vertex degree corresponding to dual face degree. Color: #00FFFF.
Flash both graphs to emphasize the duality. Color: #FFD700.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Crucial for printed circuit board design.
Useful for coloring maps and networks.
animations: Show a printed circuit board diagram. Color: #FFFFFF.
Superimpose the dual graph on the circuit map. Color: #FFD700.
Label the nodes as components to show practical utility. Color: #00FF00.
